title: Pendle PT capital requirements decay continuously toward the underlying asset's charge as maturity approaches
content:
A.3.2.2.1.1.1.2.1.1.1.3.2 specifies a capital charge as a function of block time:

`Instance Financial CRR = initialValue - ((currentTime - startTime) * decayRatePerSecond)`

with `initialValue` = 10% at exactly six months to maturity (A.3.2.2.1.1.1.2.1.1.1.3.2.1), `startTime` the block timestamp six months before expiry, and `decayRatePerSecond = totalDecay / totalDuration`. The terminal value is pinned by argument rather than by fiat: A.3.2.2.1.1.1.2.1.1.1.3.2.4.1.1 sets the Final Value to the Direct Ethena Exposure CRR of 3%, "since the PT is convertible into the underlying asset at this point."

So the schedule expresses a specific claim about what a Pendle Principal Token is: a duration wrapper on an underlying asset. The excess charge above 3% is pure duration risk, and it amortizes to zero exactly when the wrapper does. Nothing about the counterparty changes; only the time an Agent is locked into it.

A.3.2.2.1.1.1.2.1.1.1.3.1 truncates the curve rather than extending it: PTs with more than six months to maturity "require 100% Instance Total CRR" — the full-reservation charge that makes a position economically impossible. Sky is not pricing long duration expensively; it is refusing it, using the capital charge as the enforcement mechanism instead of a prohibition.

The design's notable property is that it is *computable without judgment*. Both inputs are on-chain (`currentTime` is "the timestamp of the current Ethereum block"; expiry is a PT constant), so an Agent's requirement updates every block with no reassessment, no committee and no dispute. Compare this with the discretionary machinery elsewhere in the framework — flat administered CRRs, per-deployment approvals, event-classification judgments. Where the risk is purely a function of time, the Atlas writes a formula.

A.3.2.2.1.1.1.2.1.1.1.3.3 adds the concentration backstop in the same currency: Pendle Ethena Exposures beyond 20% of an Agent's total Allocation System Investments require 100% Instance Total CRR.
description: Inside six months the CRR falls linearly per second from 10% to the 3% Direct Ethena charge; beyond six months to maturity the position requires 100% CRR and is effectively unusable.
